Description: SwiftUI views are lightweight value types rebuilt on every state change
Do: Keep view structs small and focused
Don't: Put heavy logic or storage in view body
Code Good: struct ProfileCard: View { let user: User; var body: some View { VStack { Text(user.name) } } }
Code Bad: class ProfileCard: View { // classes are wrong for SwiftUI views }

Description: Break complex views into smaller composable pieces
Do: Extract computed properties and subview structs
Don't: One massive body with 200+ lines
Code Good: var header: some View { HStack { avatar; nameLabel } }
Code Bad: var body: some View { // 300 lines of nested stacks }

Description: Custom ViewModifiers encapsulate repeated style patterns
Do: Create modifiers for card styles button styles etc
Don't: Repeating the same modifier chain everywhere
Code Good: struct CardStyle: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View { content.padding().background(.background).cornerRadius(12).shadow(radius: 4) } }
Code Bad: .padding().background(.background).cornerRadius(12).shadow(radius: 4) // repeated 20x

Description: ViewBuilder enables if/else and switch in view composition
Do: @ViewBuilder for computed properties returning conditional views
Don't: Wrapping everything in AnyView for type erasure
Code Good: @ViewBuilder var content: some View { if isLoggedIn { Dashboard() } else { LoginView() } }
Code Bad: AnyView(isLoggedIn ? AnyView(Dashboard()) : AnyView(LoginView())) // performance hit

Description: Each stack type serves a specific layout direction
Do: VStack for vertical HStack for horizontal ZStack for overlay
Don't: Nesting unnecessary stacks
Code Bad: VStack { HStack { VStack { Text(title) } } } // unnecessary nesting

Guideline: Use LazyVStack and LazyHStack for long lists
Description: Lazy stacks only create views that are visible on screen
Do: LazyVStack inside ScrollView for lists over 20 items
Don't: Regular VStack for hundreds of items
Code Good: ScrollView { LazyVStack { ForEach(items) { item in ItemRow(item: item) } } }
Code Bad: ScrollView { VStack { ForEach(items) { ... } } } // creates all 1000 views

Description: Grid provides flexible row and column based layouts
Do: Grid with GridRow for tables and aligned content
Don't: Nested HStacks trying to align columns
Code Good: Grid { GridRow { Text('Name'); Text('Score') } GridRow { Text('Alice'); Text('95') } }
Code Bad: VStack { HStack { Text('Name'); Spacer(); Text('Score') } } // misaligned

Description: Spacer pushes content to edges within stacks
Do: One Spacer to push content to opposite end
Don't: Multiple Spacers creating unclear layouts
Code Bad: HStack { Spacer(); Text(title); Spacer(); Button('Edit') {}; Spacer() }

Description: Consistent spacing creates visual rhythm
Do: Standard spacing values: 4 8 12 16 20 24 32
Don't: Arbitrary spacing values that break rhythm
Code Bad: .padding(13) .padding(.top, 7) // inconsistent

Description: GeometryReader is powerful but can cause performance issues
Do: Use only when you truly need parent dimensions
Don't: GeometryReader for simple proportional layouts
Code Bad: GeometryReader everywhere for basic centering // use alignment instead

Description: NavigationStack is the modern replacement with programmatic navigation
Do: NavigationStack with NavigationLink and navigationDestination
Don't: NavigationView which is deprecated
Code Good: NavigationStack { List { NavigationLink('Settings', value: Route.settings) }.navigationDestination(for: Route.self) { ... } }
Code Bad: NavigationView { NavigationLink(destination: SettingsView()) { Text('Settings') } }

Guideline: Use navigation path for programmatic nav
Description: NavigationPath enables push/pop from code
Do: @State private var path = NavigationPath() for navigation state
Don't: Manual isActive bindings on NavigationLinks
Code Bad: @State var showSettings = false; NavigationLink(isActive: $showSettings) // fragile

Description: TabView with tabItem for primary app navigation
Do: Tab enum with tabItem labels and images
Don't: Custom tab bars unless you need non-standard behavior
Code Bad: Custom HStack at bottom acting as tab bar // loses system features

Guideline: Use sheet and fullScreenCover for modals
Description: Present views modally with system animations
Do: .sheet for partial modals .fullScreenCover for full screen
Don't: Custom overlay views for modal presentation
Code Bad: ZStack { if showProfile { ProfileView().transition(.move(edge: .bottom)) } }

Description: @State for simple value types owned by a single view
Do: @State for toggles selections and form inputs
Don't: @State for shared or complex data
Code Bad: @State private var viewModel = ViewModel() // use @StateObject

Description: @Binding creates two-way connection to parent state
Do: @Binding for child views that modify parent state
Don't: Passing closures for simple state updates
Code Good: struct Toggle: View { @Binding var isOn: Bool }
Code Bad: struct Toggle: View { var isOn: Bool; var onToggle: (Bool) -> Void }

Description: @Observable macro replaces ObservableObject in iOS 17+
Do: @Observable class for view models and data stores
Don't: ObservableObject with @Published for new projects
Code Bad: class UserStore: ObservableObject { @Published var users: [User] = [] } // old pattern

Description: Environment values for shared dependencies and settings
Do: @Environment for color scheme locale and custom dependencies
Don't: Singletons or global state
Code Bad: let colorScheme = UITraitCollection.current.userInterfaceStyle // UIKit bridge

Description: Keep state as local as possible
Do: Lift state only when multiple views need it
Don't: Global state for view-specific data
Code Good: // State lives in the view that owns it @State private var isExpanded = false
Code Bad: // Global store for a single view's toggle AppState.shared.isCardExpanded

Description: System colors adapt to dark mode and accessibility
Do: Color.primary Color.secondary Color.accentColor
Don't: .red .blue fixed colors that don't adapt
Code Bad: Text(title).foregroundColor(.black) // breaks in dark mode

Description: 2500+ built-in icons that match system typography
Do: Image(systemName:) with symbol rendering modes
Don't: Custom icon assets for standard UI actions
Code Bad: Image('custom-heart') // doesn't match system style

Description: SwiftUI materials create frosted glass effects
Do: .ultraThinMaterial .regularMaterial .thickMaterial
Don't: Custom blur effects or fixed semi-transparent colors
Code Bad: backgroundColor: UIColor.systemBackground.withAlphaComponent(0.8) // UIKit bridge

Description: Gradients shadows and materials as shape styles
Do: LinearGradient AngularGradient and custom ShapeStyles
Don't: Hardcoded colors for decorative backgrounds
Code Bad: .fill(Color.blue) // flat when gradient would be better

Description: .font(.system(.title design: .rounded)) for visual character
Do: Font designs: .default .rounded .serif .monospaced
Don't: Custom fonts when system fonts would work
Code Bad: Font.custom('Avenir', size: 24) // when system rounded is enough

Description: Wrap state mutations in withAnimation for implicit animation
Do: withAnimation(.spring()) for natural bouncy transitions
Don't: Animate everything or nothing
Code Bad: isExpanded.toggle() // instant state change no animation

Description: Shared element transitions between views
Do: matchedGeometryEffect for hero transitions between views
Don't: Manual frame calculation for element transitions
Code Good: @Namespace var animation; Image(photo).matchedGeometryEffect(id: photo.id, in: animation)
Code Bad: Custom position animation trying to match elements across views

Description: Haptic feedback for interactions in iOS 17+
Do: .sensoryFeedback for impact selection and notification
Don't: UIImpactFeedbackGenerator from UIKit
Code Bad: let generator = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style: .medium); generator.impactOccurred()

Description: PhaseAnimator creates sequenced animation phases
Do: PhaseAnimator for loading indicators and attention effects
Don't: Multiple chained DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter
Code Bad: @State var scale = 1.0; onAppear { DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter { scale = 1.2 } }

Description: Springs feel more natural than linear or easeInOut
Do: .spring() with custom response and dampingFraction
Don't: Linear animations for UI elements
Code Bad: .animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: isExpanded) // robotic feel

Guideline: Use List for platform-native scrolling lists
Description: List provides system styling pull-to-refresh and swipe actions
Do: List with ForEach for dynamic data
Don't: ScrollView + LazyVStack when you want system list features
Code Good: List { ForEach(items) { item in ItemRow(item: item).swipeActions { Button(role: .destructive) { delete(item) } { Text('Delete') } } } }
Code Bad: ScrollView { LazyVStack { ForEach(items) { ... } } } // no swipe actions or separators

Description: Section with header and footer for organized lists
Do: Section for categorized data with clear headers
Don't: Flat lists with manual separator views
Code Bad: List { Text('Recent').font(.headline); ForEach(recent) { ... }; Text('All').font(.headline) }

Description: searchable modifier adds native search bar
Do: searchable(text:) for filterable lists
Don't: Custom TextField at top of list for search
Code Bad: VStack { TextField('Search', text: $query); List { ... } } // not native

Guideline: Use Form for settings and input screens
Description: Form provides system-grouped styling for settings
Do: Form with sections for settings screens
Don't: VStack with manual styling for form layouts
Code Good: Form { Section('Profile') { TextField('Name', text: $name); Toggle('Notifications', isOn: $notifs) } }
Code Bad: VStack { Text('Name'); TextField('', text: $name).textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder) }

Description: Set keyboard type for input context
Do: keyboardType textContentType for smart input
Don't: Generic keyboard for all inputs
Code Bad: TextField('Email', text: $email) // default keyboard, no autofill

Description: Every interactive element needs an accessible description
Do: Label or accessibilityLabel on all buttons and controls
Don't: Icon-only buttons without labels
Code Bad: Button { Image(systemName: 'trash') } // VoiceOver says 'trash'

Description: Text should scale with user's preferred text size
Do: Use system font styles that respect Dynamic Type
Don't: .font(.system(size: 16)) which doesn't scale
Code Bad: .font(.system(size: 16)) // fixed size ignores user preference

Description: Group related elements into single accessible unit
Do: Combine related label + value into one VoiceOver element
Don't: Every text being a separate VoiceOver stop
Code Bad: // VoiceOver reads: 'Name' then 'Alice' as separate elements

Guideline: Use task over onAppear for async
Description: task modifier handles async lifecycle correctly
Do: .task for data loading and async work on appear
Don't: .onAppear with Task { } for async work
Code Bad: .onAppear { Task { await viewModel.loadData() } } // manual Task creation

Description: SwiftUI redraws views when observed state changes
Do: Use Equatable let properties to prevent redraws
Don't: @State or @Observable for data that doesn't change
Code Good: struct ItemRow: View { let item: Item // value type, only redraws if item changes }
Code Bad: struct ItemRow: View { @State var item: Item // unnecessary reactivity }

Description: @Previewable creates state bindings in previews
Do: @Previewable @State for interactive previews
Don't: Static previews or manual preview wrappers
Code Bad: struct Preview: View { @State var isOn = false; var body: some View { Toggle('Notify', isOn: $isOn) } }
